gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 'up to 2.5 hours' battery figure for these mini projectors is only reached in ECO mode. ProjectorCentral measured the XGIMI MoGo 4 at 151 ISO lumens in ECO. That is about 38% of its 400-lumen Performance mode and about a third of the 450 ISO lumens XGIMI advertises. In Standard mode (258 lumens) it lasted about 90 minutes.
standout_why: Compared against these rival pages: itechguides MoGo 4 vs Capsule 3 (rank 8), Expert Reviews best portable projector (rank 4), a2zcheck best mini projectors (rank 3) and ChatGPT's own answer. itechguides and a2zcheck say the 2.5 h claim is an Eco-mode figure. Expert Reviews says only that battery life is 'around two hours in low-brightness modes'. None of them gives a lumen figure for Eco or battery use, says how much dimmer Eco is, or gives a Standard-mode runtime. ChatGPT's answer pairs '450 ISO lumens' with 'built-in battery' as though you get both at once. I could not open the Wirecutter page (the cited proxy only shows an anti-bot notice and nytimes.com is blocked). TechRadar and RTINGS came back without their pick text, so I could not check those three.
decides: This confirms the MoGo 4 as the battery pick, but only with a caveat. Unplugged, a full-length film in full brightness is not realistic: you get about 151 lumens for about 2.5 h, or 258 lumens for about 90 minutes. A brighter battery film needs the $129 PowerBase Stand, which XGIMI rates at up to 5 h. The Capsule 3 has the same trade-off. Expert Reviews' Stuart Andrews got about 2.5 h only in the 'dimmer Eco mode' and 60 to 80 minutes at full brightness. Shoppers who will be near a socket should treat the battery as a convenience and pick on brightness when plugged in.

findings.label: Measured brightness by power mode (Standard colour mode)
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review – ProjectorCentral
findings.note: ISO 21118 measurements, review dated 2025-08-25. Other colour modes: ECO 153–154, Standard 258–270, Performance 402–404. The reviewer advises against Performance mode because it has a green cast. ECO is 151/400 = 38% of Performance and 151/450 = 34% of XGIMI's rated 450 ISO lumens. The review does not say whether it measured on battery or AC.

findings.label: Battery runtime by power mode
findings.value: About 2.5 h in ECO; about 90 min in Standard
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review – ProjectorCentral
findings.note: ProjectorCentral says the projector is 'rated to last for up to 2.5 hours when playing video content in ECO mode'. In its test, Standard power mode lasted through War of the Worlds (90 min) and ECO ran about 2.5 h. Video playback, with the 72 Wh internal battery.

findings.label: Fan noise by power mode, front of unit
findings.value: 48.2 dBA Performance; 32.2 dBA Standard; 31.2 dBA ECO
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review – ProjectorCentral
findings.note: Measured about 3 ft from each side in a room with a 30.5 dBA noise floor. Loudest Performance reading was 52.4 dBA on the left side. XGIMI rates 28 dBA in lab conditions. This can fill the 'Not measured yet' fan cell on our page.

findings.label: Maker playtime table, Standard vs Eco
findings.value: Capsule 3 (D2425): Standard >2 h, Eco >3 h. Mars 3 Air (D2325): Standard >2 h, Eco >2.5 h

findings.note: Nebula says the data 'was collected in laboratory conditions, and therefore is totally theoretical data'. For Google TV models, Eco is under Settings > Display & Sound > Picture > Brightness. Nebula notes: 'To stay in Eco mode, make sure you disable the Auto mode when the unit is plugged into power.' I matched D2425 to the 200-lumen Google TV Capsule 3 from a soundcore AU URL in a search result that I did not open.
